hero.title: AWS architecture.
hero.lead: Share the platform. Isolate Dev and Prod. Deploy networking, security, containers and data with Terraform modules and commented configuration.
foundation.title: Share the common ground. Isolate what matters.
foundation.lead: A shared foundation for Dev and Prod, with applications, identities and data kept separate. Sharing fixed resources avoids duplication; savings depend on your workload.
foundation.shared.detail: ECR for application images, WAF rules for public entry points, an installation budget and encrypted Terraform state.
foundation.isolated: Each environment has its own space.
foundation.isolated.detail: VPC, CloudFront, Next.js on S3, internal ALB, Fargate and Cognito. Choose RDS PostgreSQL, Aurora PostgreSQL/MySQL or DocumentDB. Optional SQS and worker.
architecture.title: An architecture you can walk through.
architecture.lead: Select a component to understand its purpose, access controls and the module that creates it.
architecture.note: WAF protects web and API entry. Data and events use their own IAM and network controls. On mobile, pan the diagram or select Dev/Prod.
reference.eyebrow: 05 / TRY THE ARCHITECTURE WITH AN EXAMPLE
reference.title: Luma. An example on your architecture.
reference.lead: The solution includes a replaceable application to test the end-to-end path: Next.js frontend, Node.js API and private data. This lab simulates its logic; the product includes all the source.
lab.title: What if the queue is unavailable?
lab.lead: When SQS is enabled, the request and its event are committed together. This lab shows failed delivery recovery without duplicate activity.
lab.disclaimer: A browser simulation. It reuses the included domain logic; it does not call AWS or store personal data.
lab.label: Your sample request
modules.title: Modules you can understand and adapt.
modules.lead: Each module has its own inputs and outputs. The application is a replaceable example; the infrastructure is the foundation for your next project.
modules.resources: Explore the resources created by each module
start.title: Configuration you can read.
start.lead: Commented examples for Dev, Prod and a separate demo. Real account metadata, plans and runtime artifacts stay outside Git.
start.step1.detail: Open Luma on localhost. The demo uses memory and does not consume AWS.
start.step2.detail: Edit region, capacity, portals and data protection in the commented tfvars.
start.step3.detail: Use an AWS SSO session. The CLI applies saved plans, publishes images and runs the private migration.
start.production: For Prod: a domain and ACM certificate, quota review and a restore test. Deployments create billable resources; the budget notifies and does not stop spending.
costs.title: Choose capacity with context.
costs.lead: Share the foundation and size each environment. The database, ALB, private endpoints and Fargate incur charges even when the application receives no requests.
costs.link: Read about costs and capacity decisions
family.title: More building blocks for your platform.
family.nexus: The modular application platform for Azure.
family.inventory: Inventory, cost analysis and visibility for your Azure resources.
closing.title: Start with a clear architecture. Build your solution.
footer.text: A modular architecture for building on AWS.
footer.independent: An independent community project. Not an official Amazon Web Services product.
database.title: Your data, your choice.
database.lead: The architecture supports four data profiles. Terraform wires the application adapter, private port and permissions for the selected engine.
database.boundary: API and worker use roles. Initial administration uses an AWS-managed secret. Readers incur costs and do not replace backups.
demo.label: LUMA · INTERACTIVE DEMO
demo.subtitle: Explore the base flow. Enable events when you need them.
demo.title: Create. Explore. Verify.
demo.lead: Submit a request and switch users. Each sees their own records; the operator can inspect the team.
demo.failure.detail: Enable SQS, save a request with an offline queue, then recover it.
demo.disclaimer: Fictional data in memory. It reuses the product domain logic and never calls AWS. In a real deployment, the API validates identity and permissions.
hero.map.title: One platform. Two environments.
hero.map.shared.detail: Images · web protection · state and budget
hero.map.note: Logical view · each environment owns its VPC
hero.view.default.title: Created once. Used by two environments.
hero.view.default.copy: ECR, WAF, state and budget are shared. Each environment owns its network, applications, identity and data.
